summary: Gauri Viswanathan is a scholar of Indology who studied at the University of Delhi (BA, MA) and Columbia University (PhD). She taught English at the University of Delhi (~1973–1978) and became a humanities professor and South Asia Institute director at Columbia (~1989).

Gaurinath Sastri was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (~1957–1970), Philological Secretary of The Asiatic Society (attested 1959), and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1970–1976), teaching Gustav Roth.

Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Elphinstone College (~1884–1887) and under Bhagwanlal Indraji (~1887–1888), and he later taught Bisheshwar Nath Reu.

Gavin D'Costa is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Cambridge and Birmingham (~1981–1985). He taught at the West London Institute (~1985–1988) and became Emeritus Professor of Catholic Theology at the University of Bristol (1993).

Gavin Flood, an Indology and religious studies scholar, studied at Lancaster University under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. He held posts at Lampeter, Stirling, and Oxford, and served as the Yap Kim Hao Professor at Yale-NUS College in 2016.
Geetha K. Wilson is an Indology doctoral student and faculty member at the University of Tübingen, studying under doctoral supervisor Claire Maes (attested 2026).

Gelek is a Tibetology scholar who served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998) and held posts as a visiting lecturer at the University of California and a visiting scholar at Oxford.

Gelek Rimpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. Educated at Drepung Monastery, Young Lamas Home School, and Cornell, he directed Tibet House in New Delhi (1965) and founded Jewel Heart (1988), teaching Robert A. F. Thurman.

Gembo Dorji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, receiving instruction from traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup and Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima.

Gen'ichi Yamazaki was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who earned his degrees, including a doctorate, at the University of Tokyo. He served as a researcher at Toyo Bunko (~1965–1975) and as a professor at Kokugakuin University (2006).

Gendun Chopel was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Drisha, Labrang, Kumbum, and Drepung monasteries under Gendun Tendzin Gyatso and Sherab Gyatso. He taught Rakra Tethong Rinpoche and Nyak Rongpa Dawa Zangpo.
Gendun Chophel was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Sherab Gyatso (~1921–1927). He was affiliated with the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941 and taught Horkhang Sonam Palbar.

Gendun Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who founded Dhagpo Kagyu Ling and served as its abbot and retreat master (~1977–1997). He also founded three other Dhagpo centers and taught Shenpen Hookham and Henrik Havlat.

Genjun Sasaki was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who graduated from Kyoto University and studied under Tokuryu Yamauchi and others. He served as a professor at Otani University, a Fulbright professor at Harvard, and a visiting professor at Hamburg.
Genro was an 18th-century Buddhist studies figure who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku and held the post of dai-ichiza at Myoshin-ji.
Genryu Kagoshima was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1931–1934). He later served as a professor at Komazawa University (~1957–1983) and taught William M. Bodiford.

Gensho Imanari was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned undergraduate, graduate, and PhD degrees at Waseda University. He served as an assistant professor at Kokushikan University (~1965–1970) and professor emeritus at Rissho University (1980–1996).
Genshu Watanabe was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University and trained under Sogaku Harada, becoming his dharma heir.
Genzao was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology practitioner who studied under Jiangze Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche, completing studies at Dzogchen Monastery by 1950.

Geo Widengren was an Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies scholar educated at Stockholm and Uppsala under Henrik Samuel Nyberg. He was a professor of religious history at Uppsala (1940–1973) and served as president of the IAHR (~1960–1970).
